title: The Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation Side Effect Scale (NIBS-SES): development of a brief, multilingual questionnaire for monitoring adverse effects in transcranial magnetic, electrical and ultrasound stimulation
title_zh: 非侵入性脑刺激副作用量表 (NIBS-SES)：用于监测经颅磁、电和超声刺激不良反应的简短多语言问卷
abstract: BACKGROUND: Monitoring of adverse effects in neuromodulation relies largely on non-standardized or time-consuming instruments, limiting comparison of tolerability within and across transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial electrical stimulation (tES), and transcranial ultrasound stimulation (tUS). We developed the Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation Side Effect Scale (NIBS-SES), a brief questionnaire for repeated assessment of adverse effects. METHODS: The NIBS-SES was designed iteratively, with an initial version evaluated in 44 patients receiving TMS for major depression to assess repeated-use feasibility and adverse-effect patterns. Items were expanded based on a literature review of adverse-effect prevalences across TMS, tES, and tUS (n = 6415 individuals) and refined by 12 NIBS experts. The final version was professionally translated into 15 languages (Arabic, Basque, Catalan, Dutch, French, Galician, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin Chinese, Persian, Portuguese, Spanish). RESULTS: Patient-reported adverse effects across 851 sessions declined despite titration of stimulation intensity. Prior-session occurrence was the strongest predictor of current-session reports (β = 4.73, p < .001), detectable only through repeated session-level assessment. Adverse effects during and between sessions showed different patterns of persistence, supporting their separate assessment. The literature review revealed substantial overlap across neuromodulation modalities, supporting a unified instrument. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support the feasibility of repeated session-level assessment with the initial version, from which the final NIBS-SES was derived. This multilingual, open-access instrument comprises 10 within-session and 9 between-session items developed for monitoring across TMS, tES, and tUS (for questionnaire and digital implementation files, see OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/XZ3NB). Validation across brain stimulation modalities, protocols, and clinical populations will require prospective multi-site data.
abstract_zh: 背景：在神经调控中监测不良反应主要依赖非标准化或耗时的仪器，这限制了在经颅磁刺激 (TMS)、经颅电刺激 (tES) 和经颅超声刺激 (tUS) 体内外对耐受性的比较。我们开发了非侵入性脑刺激副作用量表 (NIBS-SES)，这是一个简短的问卷，用于反复评估不良反应。方法：NIBS-SES 采用迭代方式设计，初版在 44 名接受 TMS 治疗重度抑郁的患者中进行评估，以评估重复使用的可行性和不良反应模式。基于对 TMS、tES 和 tUS 6415 名个体文献中不良反应患病率的文献综述，对项目进行了扩展，并由 12 名 NIBS 专家进行了完善。最终版本由专业人员翻译成 15 种语言（阿拉伯语、巴斯克语、加泰罗尼亚语、荷兰语、法语、加利西亚语、德语、印地语、意大利语、日语、韩语、普通话、波斯语、葡萄牙语、西班牙语）。结果：在 851 次会话中，尽管刺激强度进行了调整，但患者报告的不良反应有所下降。先前会话的出现是当前会话报告的最强预测因子 (β = 4.73, p < .001)，仅通过反复的会话级别评估才能检测到。会话内和会话间的不良反应表现出不同的持续性模式，支持其单独评估。文献综述揭示了各种神经调控模式之间存在 substantial overlap，支持统一的仪器。结论：我们的研究结果支持使用初版进行反复会话级别评估，从中得出了最终的 NIBS-SES。该多语言公开获取的仪器包含 10 个会话内和 9 个会话间项目，旨在监测 TMS、tES 和 tUS (如需问卷和数字实现文件，请访问 OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/XZ3NB) 。需要前瞻性多中心数据来验证跨脑刺激模式、方案和临床人群的效果。
